questions.stem: Which type of rural settlement has closely built houses in one cluster and is common in fertile alluvial plains?
options: Isolated farmstead standing alone among the fields
questions.explanation: In a compact or nucleated settlement houses are built close together around a common area, with farmland outside. It is common where fertile land and water are available, as in alluvial plains. Hence the correct answer is: Compact (nucleated) settlement.

optionRationale.1: In a dispersed settlement houses are far apart.
optionRationale.2: A hamleted settlement is split into physically separate units.
optionRationale.3: An isolated farmstead is a single house among fields.

questions.stem: A rural settlement divided into several units that are physically separated but bear a common name is called
questions.explanation: In a hamleted settlement a village is divided into several separate hamlets with a common village name. Each hamlet may be occupied by a different community. This pattern is common in the Ganga plain and in Chhattisgarh.

optionRationale.2: A compact settlement is a single cluster.
optionRationale.3: A dispersed settlement has scattered houses without a common cluster.
optionRationale.4: A linear settlement is described by its pattern along a road or river.

questions.stem: Most people in a rural settlement depend mainly on
options: banking and finance services in the market towns
manufacturing in large factories in the cities
quaternary activities such as research and information work
questions.explanation: Rural people earn their living mostly from land-based primary activities such as farming, animal rearing, fishing and forestry. Banking, large factories and knowledge services are typical of towns. Hence the correct answer is: primary activities such as agriculture.

optionRationale.1: Banking is a tertiary activity found mainly in towns.
optionRationale.4: Quaternary activities are knowledge-based and mainly urban.

questions.objective: Describe the economic base of villages

questions.stem: A town whose main function is to serve as the seat of government is called an
questions.explanation: Administrative towns house the offices of the government, such as national or state capitals and district headquarters. Industrial, mining and port towns take their name from the activity that drives them. Hence the correct answer is: administrative town.

optionRationale.2: Mining towns depend on mineral extraction.
optionRationale.4: Port towns depend on handling cargo.

questions.stem: A common problem of rapidly growing cities in India is
options: a fall in the number of vehicles
the growth of slums and a shortage of housing
questions.explanation: Large numbers of migrants reach cities faster than houses, water and sewers can be built. This produces overcrowding, slums and pressure on services. The other statements describe the opposite of the actual situation.

optionRationale.1: There is a shortage of housing, not a surplus.
optionRationale.3: Open space is scarce in big cities.

questions.stem: In urban geography, a conurbation is best described as
options: a continuous built-up urban area formed by the merging of several towns or cities
a single large village with several scattered hamlets around it, linked by footpaths
a small town with fewer than 5,000 persons living in a compact area
a group of villages situated around a lake
questions.explanation: The term conurbation was coined by Patrick Geddes in 1915. It describes an extensive urban area formed when towns and cities grow together into a continuous built-up area. Hence the correct answer is: a continuous built-up urban area formed by the merging of several towns or cities.

optionRationale.3: A town of that size would not be a conurbation.

questions.stem: The 'situation' of a settlement refers to
options: the actual piece of land on which it is built, including its soil and slope
its location in relation to the surrounding areas and routes
the number of people who live and work in it, and how that has changed
the type and material of the houses used in it
questions.explanation: Site means the actual ground on which a settlement is built, while situation means its position in relation to other places, routes, resources and the surrounding region. A good situation helps a settlement grow.

optionRationale.1: That is the definition of site.

questions.stem: The semi-compact (fragmented) type of rural settlement is commonly found in
options: the hilly forests of Meghalaya and Uttarakhand
the arid and cold interior of Ladakh
the Gujarat plain and parts of Rajasthan
the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans delta
questions.explanation: Semi-compact settlements result from the tendency of a dominant community to cluster while other groups live apart. They are common in the Gujarat plain and parts of Rajasthan, according to NCERT. Hence the correct answer is: the Gujarat plain and parts of Rajasthan.

optionRationale.1: Meghalaya is known for dispersed settlements.
optionRationale.2: Ladakh has sparse and scattered settlements.
optionRationale.4: The Sundarbans have very few settlements.

questions.stem: In Census terms, an urban agglomeration is
options: a group of villages bearing a common name
only the central municipal area of a city
a large village that holds a weekly market
a town together with its adjoining urban outgrowths
questions.explanation: An urban agglomeration is an urban area that includes a town and its adjoining urban outgrowths such as railway colonies, university campuses and suburbs. It therefore covers more than the central municipal limits.

optionRationale.2: That describes only the core, not the outgrowths.
optionRationale.3: A village with a market remains rural.

questions.stem: In the Census classification of Indian towns by population, towns with 20,000 to 49,999 persons belong to
questions.explanation: Class I towns have 1,00,000 or more persons, Class II have 50,000 to 99,999 and Class III have 20,000 to 49,999. Class IV has 10,000 to 19,999 and Class V has 5,000 to 9,999.

optionRationale.2: Class I has 1,00,000 or more persons.

questions.stem: A district had 60 lakh people of whom 24 lakh were urban. A decade later the total was 80 lakh and the urban population was 36 lakh. By how many percentage points did the urban share rise?
questions.explanation: The first urban share is 24 divided by 60, or 40 per cent. The second is 36 divided by 80, or 45 per cent. The share therefore rose by 5 percentage points. Hence the correct answer is: 5 percentage points.

optionRationale.1: 12 is the rise in lakh, not in share.
optionRationale.4: 4 does not match the calculated shares.

questions.objective: Compute the change in urban share

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Large cities attract many migrants from rural areas.
Reason (R): Cities offer a wider range of jobs, education and health services.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Cities concentrate industry, trade and services, so they offer a wider range of jobs, schools, colleges and hospitals than villages do. These pull factors attract rural people, which is why the reason correctly explains the assertion and option 1 is right.

optionRationale.2: R is the direct explanation of A.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Rural settlements have no non-agricultural activities.
Reason (R): In many villages artisans, traders and service providers also earn their living.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Agriculture is the main activity in villages, but many villagers also work as artisans, shopkeepers, transporters and service providers. So the claim that villages have no non-agricultural activity is false, while the reason is true, and option 4 is correct.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so R cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so option 2 is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so option 3 is wrong.

questions.objective: Describe the economic activities in villages

questions.stem: Match List-I (type of rural settlement) with List-II (area where commonly found, as per NCERT).

right: I. Fertile alluvial plains and north-eastern states
II. Gujarat plain and parts of Rajasthan
III. Chhattisgarh and lower valleys of the Himalaya
IV. Meghalaya, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala

questions.explanation: Compact settlements are common in fertile plains and the north-east (I), semi-compact in the Gujarat plain and parts of Rajasthan (II), hamleted in Chhattisgarh and lower Himalayan valleys (III), and dispersed in Meghalaya, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala (IV).

optionRationale.1: It swaps compact and semi-compact types.
optionRationale.2: It swaps semi-compact and hamleted types.

right: I. Actual ground on which a settlement is built
II. Location in relation to surroundings and routes
III. Merging of several towns into a continuous built-up area
IV. A town together with its adjoining urban outgrowths

questions.explanation: Site is the actual ground (I), situation is the relative location (II), conurbation is a merged continuous urban area (III) and an urban agglomeration is a town with its outgrowths (IV).

optionRationale.2: It swaps conurbation and urban agglomeration.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about the functional classification of towns.
A. Mining towns grow near mineral deposits.
B. Port towns handle trade and transport of goods.
C. Cantonment towns are built mainly for the army.
D. A town can have only one function.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Mining towns grow near mineral deposits, port towns handle trade and transport, and cantonment towns are built mainly for the army, so A, B and C are correct. A town often performs several functions, as many large cities do, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out C, which is correct.
optionRationale.3: Option 3 includes D, which is wrong, and leaves out A.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes D, which is wrong.

questions.objective: Review the functional classification of towns

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about urban terms.
A. A conurbation is formed when towns grow together into a continuous urban area.
B. The term conurbation was introduced by Patrick Geddes.
C. An urban agglomeration includes a town and its adjoining urban outgrowths.
D. All rural settlements have the same size and pattern.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A conurbation forms when towns grow together into a continuous urban area, a term introduced by Patrick Geddes, and an urban agglomeration is a town with its adjoining urban outgrowths, so A, B and C are correct. Rural settlements differ widely in size and pattern, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Option 1 leaves out B, which is correct.
optionRationale.2: Option 2 includes D, which is wrong.
optionRationale.4: Option 4 includes D, which is wrong.

questions.stem: Houses built of bamboo and wood on raised platforms in heavy-rainfall regions show that rural house types are shaped mainly by
options: the size of the nearest city
the distance from the state capital
questions.explanation: House form reflects the environment. Heavy rain and floods lead to raised floors and sloping roofs, and builders use local material such as bamboo, wood, mud or stone. Distance and language do not decide house structure.

optionRationale.2: City size does not decide house form.
optionRationale.3: Language does not decide house form.
optionRationale.4: Distance from the capital does not decide house form.

questions.objective: Relate rural house types to the environment
